articles.title: Massive fire erupts in jet fuel unit at Chevron's LA refinery
articles.content: STORY: A massive fire erupted at Chevron’s El Segundo refinery near Los Angeles on Thursday.Chevron said there were no injuries and all workers were accounted for…But it did raise questions over fuel supply in California, an isolated energy market. The fire broke out in a jet fuel production unit, which supplies the Los Angeles International Airport (LAX).It’s not immediately clear how it started. A source said it was also unclear if the incident had impacted the refinery’s ability to produce fuel - or whether fuel already stored there was affected. Tamara Smith, a local resident, said it was a scary moment.“I heard a little explosion. It sounded like the start of a 3.0 earthquake. And then a second later, there was another loud explosion, and it felt like a 5.(0) earthquake and I thought we were actually having the start of an earthquake. It’s Chevron's second biggest refinery in the U.S.; it supplies a fifth of all motor vehicle fuels and 40% of the jet fuel consumed in southern California.Analysts said it’s unlikely to impact wider oil prices, but due to isolation from other refining centers, the state’s gasoline prices could rise.In addition to Chevron, state and federal safety agencies will investigate the fire after the blaze is extinguished.

articles.title: Exclusive-Chevron exports of Venezuelan oil halved under new US authorization, sources say
articles.content: HOUSTON (Reuters) -U.S. oil major Chevron is only able to export about half the crude its joint ventures produce in Venezuela with the latest rules laid out by Washington, three sources close to the matter said. The Treasury Department in late July issued a restricted authorization allowing Chevron to operate in the sanctioned country and export oil to the U.S., but it banned payments in any currency to the government of President Nicolas Maduro. To comply with the permit, the joint ventures where the Houston-based company participates have been paying royalties and taxes with oil in kind, effectively reducing what Chevron can export to about 50% of the 240,000 barrels per day of crude the projects produce, the sources said.

articles.title: Chevron, Israeli pipeline operator to kickstart new gas pipeline to Egypt
articles.content: Chevron has signed a deal with state-owned pipeline operator Israel Natural Gas Lines to kickstart construction of the Nitzana natural gas pipeline to transport gas from the Leviathan gasfield to Egypt, the U.S. company said on Tuesday. Nitzana would ease an energy crisis in Egypt, which has spent billions of dollars on importing liquefied natural gas and is part of a concerted effort to boost Israeli gas exports to the Arab world's most populous nation. Last month, the owners of the Leviathan natural gas field off Israel signed a $35 billion export deal to supply gas to Egypt.

articles.title: California Wants to Halt Oil Industry Exodus After Years of Climate Focus
articles.content: A year after they broke up via text, California and Chevron finally reconnected by phone. Gov. Gavin Newsom’s office made its first-ever call to Chevron’s refining chief last week, days before state lawmakers passed a bill meant to stop more oil companies from leaving California. Nathan Barankin, Newsom’s chief of staff, extolled the virtues of that bill, which could boost drilling in oil-rich Kern County, and touted the state’s decision to delay putting a cap on refiners’ profits.
